title: edge-gpu-pool-rack-surge-and-floorplan-notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick working notes for allocating GPU racks at three candidate edge colo sites (NYC-1 floor B, SEA-2 mezz, FRA-3 top level). Focus: avoid last-minute power/cooling surprises, define per-rack surge headroom, layout constraints for heavy racks, and an initial spare-pool plan. Meant to be an operational checklist + numbers we can share with datahall ops and partners.

Goals:
- Define per-rack electrical budget and recommended PDU layout for 8–12 GPU servers per rack.
- Set conservative surge headroom targets to survive peak KV-cache bursts and cold-starts (safety margin for GPU turbo + fans).
- Capture simple thermal mitigation steps for aisles with dense racks (e.g., blanking panels, baffle curtains).
- Produce a minimal spare capacity plan (hot spares + cold spares) for 6-month rollout.

High-level assumptions (borrowed from model runtime ops):
- Typical server: 2U GPU node with 4x 80GB-class GPUs (A100/RTX/Next-gen) draws 2.6–3.2 kW under steady token-generation workload.
- Dense rack config target: mix of 4x- and 8x-GPU 1U/2U nodes, nominal steady-state per-rack draw = 9.6 kW (8x 1.2 kW avg) to 12.8 kW (8x 1.6 kW).
- Use conservative peak multiplier of 1.25 for fans/boost and transient power spikes during KV-cache rebuilds.
- Power delivery at colo: most racks are offered at 20A/208V circuits (single-phase) or 60A/208V 3-phase PDUs; verify available PDUs before final layout.

Site snapshot (quick table):
- NYC-1 floor B: row depth 1200 mm, raised floor, per-rack PDUs limited to dual 30A/208V; CRAC units in pairs; local chiller capacity reported 2.1 MW.
- SEA-2 mezz: slab floor, 10 ft ceiling, higher ambient summer humidity; vendor requires 1:10 dense rack review.
- FRA-3 top level: new hall, supports 30 kW racks but chargeback higher; prefer as hot-swap capacity.

Per-rack electrical plan (recommended):
1) Baseline allowed draw: plan rack power envelope = 15 kW (steady) / 18.75 kW (peak with 1.25x).
2) PDU config: dual 60A/3-phase PDUs (A+B fed) where available. If only 30A exists, split heavy nodes across PDUs and throttle max GPUs per host.
3) Breaker reservation: request breaker capacity >= 70A per rack (208V 3-phase) at colo engagement to allow future densification.
4) Power distribution notes: use power strips rated 20A per circuit, avoid >85% continuous loading (NEC guidance) — target 70% continuous.

Cooling & airflow notes:
- Target rack inlet temp: 18–27C. For dense racks aiming >10 kW steady, classify as "hot-rack" and require aisle containment or directed rear-door cooling.
- Short-term mitigations: blanking panels, high-efficiency brush strips at floor, seal cable cutouts with grommets.
- For racks >12 kW, specify rear-door heat exchanger or local in-row cooler. Add temperature probes at 3 heights (U4, U20, U38).

Physical layout constraints and weight:
- Typical loaded rack weight: 400–700 kg depending on number of GPU servers + PDUs + cable management. Confirm raised floor load per tile >2000 kg/m^2 for dense clusters.
- Aisle clearance: minimum 1.2 m for service; recommend 1.5 m for frequent maintenance.
- Cable ladder capacity: route heavy gauge power on dedicated trays; separate HV and LV runs where possible.

Capacity math examples (for planning conversation):
- Goal: 96 GPUs at NYC-1 in initial phase using 24x 4-GPU nodes (2U).
  - Steady per-node avg = 1.4 kW -> total steady = 33.6 kW.
  - Per-rack estimate (6 nodes per rack) = 8.4 kW steady -> fits comfortably on 2x30A PDU if split, but leaves no headroom for peaks.
  - With 1.25x peak factor -> rack peak = 10.5 kW. Recommend using dual 60A PDUs instead.

Spare plan (recommended):
- Hot spares: 2 racks per site in warm-ready mode (OS image loaded, GPUs validated) for failover. Each hot spare rack should have at least 50% of production networking and PDUs mirrored.
- Cold spares: additional 6 nodes in a crate with validated firmware, stored in colocation with 24–48 hr racking SLA.
- Firmware drift: maintain a monthly baseline upgrade window and snapshot images per site.

Operational checklist to share with colo ops before ordering:
- Confirm PDU model & redundancy (A+B), request dual PDUs rated >= 60A 3-phase where possible.
- CRAC/row cooling redundancy (N+1) and chiller load report for last 12 months.
- Raised floor tile load rating or slab constraints + cooling plenum strategy.
- Network handoff rack and cross-connect checklist: fiber counts, patch panel faceplate types, and OTDR test results.
- Local fire suppression and rack-intrusion policy; confirm that rear-door coolers match local sprinkler/no-spray constraints.

Risk register (brief):
- Risk: Underestimated transient power peaks during KV cache rebuild on cold start. Mitigation: soft-start orchestration + staggered node boot and transient power monitoring.
- Risk: Aisle hot spots due to uneven load distribution. Mitigation: instrument more temperature probes and enforce even distribution of heavy nodes.
- Risk: Vendor PDUs older than 5 yrs, limited continuous rating. Mitigation: request PDU spec sheet and consider replacing on-site PDU units.

Action items (owner tags):
- Maya: consolidate exact PDU models available at each colo and attach vendor spec sheets (due 2025-11-14).
- Lucas: capture historical chiller/COP numbers for NYC-1 and SEA-2 (due 2025-11-10).
- Priya: draft brief for site ops on staggered boot orchestration and power telemetry metrics to collect (due 2025-11-07).
- Diego: check freight/elevator constraints for FRA-3 (rack width/weight limits) and report (due 2025-11-12).

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Do we standardize on 60A 3-phase PDUs for all new racks or negotiate per-site? Tradeoff: higher upfront colo charge vs simplified ops.
- Acceptable SLA for cold-spare racking (24 hr vs 72 hr) — impacts inventory distribution.
- Which telemetry retention tier to apply for edge sites vs core (cost tradeoffs in Redwood Console).

Appendix: small checklist for on-site handover (copyable):
- [ ] PDU stickers applied and circuit labeling verified.
- [ ] Temperature sensors at U4/U20/U38 reporting to monitoring.
- [ ] Blank panels installed and cable cutouts sealed.
- [ ] Load tests: perform 15 min soak at 80% expected peak and record power and inlet/outlet temps.
- [ ] Image/firmware snapshot stored in S3 with site tag.

Notes to self: keep this doc lightweight — will convert to a short spreadsheet for rack-by-rack numbers once PDUs are confirmed. This is intentionally conservative on headroom (we'd rather pay a little more on colo side than chase hot swaps).
